verbatim_locators.note: COVERAGE: whole article read; Figures 3, 5 and 9 inspected as images, Figures 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8 acquired and fingerprinted but only their legends read, so figures is captions_only and the receipt is partial. SUPPLEMENTARY UNAVAILABLE: the model reaction list is declared in supplementary materials that no surface reached (JATS carries no supplementary-material element; the PMC OA bucket lists none); the raw simulation outputs are about 50 MATLAB files of roughly 350 MB each in a Harvard Dataverse deposit (listed through the Dataverse API, not downloaded). A model has no data to check, so the negative findings rest on the stated assumptions and the paper's own clinical comparisons.

entries.proposition: DESIGN: a deterministic ODE model (159 reactions) of ONE excitatory tripartite synapse; no animal, cell, patient or WWOX datum.
entries.snippet: a system of ordinary differential equations representing 159 reactions

entries.proposition: The network drive parameters were fixed in every simulation, so the only manipulated inputs are substrate concentrations and single enzyme or transporter rate constants.
entries.snippet: The critical parameters ν, ϵ, and ζ were NOT varied for any of the simulations in this work

entries.proposition: The pathological readout (Regime E, brief UP/DOWN bursts) is a speculated correlate of seizure activity, not a measured one.
entries.snippet: It was speculated that the pattern of rapid bursts of firing and quiescence could represent the synaptic-level equivalent of epileptiform electrical activity

entries.proposition: Glucose threshold for the regime change: below 3.8 mM at normal ketone, below 3.1 mM with 2 mM beta-hydroxybutyrate.
entries.snippet: the tripartite synapse system transitioned from Regime D into Regime E at a glucose concentration below 3.8 mM

entries.proposition: Figure 3a: the whole regime change is a swing of the presynaptic ATP generation rate across a dashed threshold near 1.17 x 10^6 molecules per second, against about 1.34 at baseline glucose 5 mM, a difference of roughly 13 percent. Figure 3b: the boundary is a fitted straight line y = -2.6379x + 10.327 (R squared 0.9905) through about seven points in the glucose-ketone plane.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 3, (a) ATP generation rate (10^6 molecules/s) against blood glucose 2.5 to 5 mM for beta-hydroxybutyrate 0.25 mM (blue) and 2 mM (red) with a dashed Regime D/E line; (b) beta-hydroxybutyrate against glucose with Regime D and E arrows, ketogenic-diet and normal-diet markers and a fitted line.

entries.proposition: Figure 5: low glucose (3.5 mM) with normal ketone turns long UP/DOWN states into short bursts; 2 mM ketone restores them; panel d shows the ATP rate bars (baseline about 1.34, low glucose about 1.12, low glucose with high ketone about 1.24) around the same dashed threshold. The rescue is a return across a threshold, not a quantified seizure measure.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 5, (a) baseline membrane potential trace with UP and DOWN states, (b) low glucose with brief bursts, (c) low glucose with 2 mM beta-hydroxybutyrate, (d) bar chart of ATP generation rate for baseline, low glucose normal beta-hydroxybutyrate, low glucose high beta-hydroxybutyrate with dashed Regime D/E line.

experimental_context.endpoint: membrane potential trace; ATP generation rate

entries.proposition: Pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency is rescued only when ketone reaches 4 mM; 2 mM, the ketogenic-diet level the paper uses elsewhere, does not rescue it.
entries.snippet: the system was not rescued by a β-hydroxybutyrate of 2 mM and stayed in Regime E for this concentration of ketone

entries.proposition: MCT1 deficiency is not rescued even at a ketone concentration well above the ketogenic-diet range.
entries.snippet: This was not rescued even with a concentration of β-hydroxybutyrate significantly above that typically seen in the ketogenic diet

entries.proposition: Complex I at 55 percent of baseline flips the regime and is not rescued by ketone up to 10 mM.
entries.snippet: At 55% of the baseline reaction rate constants for mitochondrial complex I

entries.proposition: Figure 9b: with complex I at 55 percent, the bars for 3.5 mM glucose with 2, 4 and 10 mM ketone (about 1.11, 1.14, 1.17) end at or just under the dashed threshold; the regime call for 10 mM rests on a bar that touches the line. Figure 9a: the 55 percent value is the point where the curve first meets the threshold.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 9, (a) ATP generation rate against mitochondrial complex I activity 100 to 50 percent of baseline with dashed Regime D/E line; (b) bars for baseline and for complex I at 55 percent under glucose 5 or 3.5 mM and beta-hydroxybutyrate 0.25, 2, 4, 10 mM.

entries.proposition: THE MODEL DISAGREES WITH THE CLINIC on the one case where it can be checked: a clinical series reports ketogenic diet effective in all eight studied complex I patients, whereas the model predicts no rescue; the authors explain this by gene-expression and biogenesis changes absent from the model.
entries.snippet: another group found that the ketogenic diet was effective for all of their studied patients with complex I deficiency

entries.proposition: The model assumes the astrocyte-neuron lactate shuttle, so the MCT1 and lactate results depend on that contested hypothesis.
entries.snippet: Our model assumes the astrocyte neuronal lactate shuttle hypothesis

entries.proposition: Kinetic parameters of a reduced model are not those of real systems, so thresholds are trends only; the authors say a real system may need 50 percent MCT1 loss where the model needs 99.5.
entries.snippet: the kinetic parameters (such as reaction rate parameters) that would result in realistic model behavior cannot be expected to be the same as those that are measured in real systems

entries.proposition: Glucose and ketone are held constant as boundary conditions, which is non-physiological.
entries.snippet: the concentration of glucose is held to be a boundary condition

entries.proposition: Competing mechanisms (gene expression, inflammation, astrocyte function, circadian, microbiota) are discussed but are NOT in the model; the model can therefore show that energy repletion is sufficient in silico, not that it is primary.
entries.snippet: It is also likely the case that the ketogenic diet has multiple diverse effects on the brain and body

entries.proposition: The authors state the energy hypothesis is a strong candidate and that other mechanisms are not excluded.
entries.snippet: We do not exclude other proposed mechanisms

entries.proposition: The study states it is computational and proposes in vivo experiments; none has been done.
A serum beta-hydroxybutyrate above about 4 mM is cited as needed for efficacy, double the 2 mM used as the ketogenic-diet value for most simulations.
entries.snippet: serum β-hydroxybutyrate levels need to be above approximately 4 mM for the ketogenic diet to be effective
